contents.text: Read the passage about Charles Darwin.

pieces.text: Charles Darwin, an English naturalist and scientist, was born on February 12, 1809. Shortly after graduating from college, he joined the crew of HMS

for a five-year survey expedition of the South American coast. This journey would prove to be one of the most important voyages in the history of science—Darwin's observations from his travels led him to publish a revolutionary book entitled
in 1859, which outlined his

content.text: theory of evolution by natural selection

pieces.text: Before the book's publication, most people believed that species had remained unchanged since their creation. Yet farmers and breeders had practiced
for thousands of years, selecting plants and animals with desirable traits to produce offspring with those same traits. That meant many people held a practical understanding of
, the process by which species change over time, even if they did not understand how it worked in nature.
was groundbreaking because it proposed a logical, scientifically sound mechanism by which evolution might occur in the wild. Today, Darwin's theory is a cornerstone of evolutionary biology.

The many slight differences which appear in the offspring from the same parents,…observed in the individuals of the same species inhabiting the same confined locality, may be called individual differences.

contents.text: The steppe mammoth was an ancient mammal that lived in large grasslands called steppes more than 200,000 years ago. Here are pictures of a steppe mammoth fossil, a living walrus, and a living African elephant.

alternativeText.text: A picture of a steppe mammoth fossil skeleton. The fossil has a long, flat skull with a hole between the eyes and two large tusks curving upwards from the mouth. Its front and back legs are long, holding its wide torso high above the ground. Each foot has short, stocky toes.

A picture of a walrus laying on ice. It has a relatively small head with small eyes and a short, whiskered snout. Two small tusks curve down from its mouth. It has a large, round body that tapers to a pair of hind flippers held close together. It has two short front flippers. Its large torso is resting on the ice beneath it.

A picture of an African elephant on dusty soil. It has wrinkly skin. It has a large head with small eyes, large, flat ears, a long trunk extending downward, and two moderately large tusks that curve upwards from its mouth. It has four long legs holding its large torso high above the ground. Each foot has short, stocky toes.

textContent.text: Peppered moths spend most of the day resting on branches and tree trunks. Some peppered moths have light-colored wings, and others have dark-colored wings.

These wing colors can camouflage the moths in their environments. This helps the moths hide from predators, such as birds. For example, a moth with light-colored wings is harder to see on light-colored bark. A moth with dark-colored wings is harder to see on dark-colored bark.

alternativeText.text: At the start, 20% of the moths in the population had light-colored wings, and 80% had dark-colored wings. At the end, 69% of the moths had light-colored wings, and 31% had dark-colored wings.

textContent.text: Pond snails live in freshwater environments such as ponds, lakes, and rivers. A pond snail's shell may be narrow or round. Each shape is better at protecting a snail against a different kind of predator.

A narrow shell provides better protection against crayfish, which attack a snail at the opening of its shell. Narrow shells have smaller openings, so snails with narrow shells are harder for crayfish to reach during an attack.

pieces.text: An
salamander can have dark-colored skin or bright-colored skin.

salamanders with bright-colored skin look similar to poisonous newts. A predator that eats a poisonous newt can get sick and die, so predators in places with poisonous newts have adapted to avoid them. Those predators may mistake salamanders with bright-colored skin for these newts. So those predators also avoid salamanders with bright-colored skin.

Since salamanders with bright-colored skin are easier to see, predators in these places are more likely to eat salamanders with bright-colored skin than salamanders with dark-colored skin.

textContent.text: Some coral snakes hunt prey like fish in the water. Others hunt prey like other snakes on land. A coral snake uses venom from its fangs to kill its prey.
